entries.question: what turn rate can this plant actually deliver?

turn_rate.note: the commanded cap is ~2x the plant's estimated turn ceiling, and the move+turn slot is infeasible at any commandable speed (walk floor 0.21 m/s => omega <= 0.01 rad/s at r_foot 1.2 m) -- so move+turn is scored relatively and every cap candidate is screened directly instead of probed

entries.question: what is the eval resolution every decision is standardised by, on the per-category suite?

decision_rule.text: Every metric is a per-category number of the suite__omni row (summarize()['cat'][c]: the median pooled over both hands of a paired category; survival = the category's own-hold survival); only the categories the candidate trained at the suite's demand are decisive (every fork trains all seven). Blocks (95 %, two-sided): F = turn: facing_closed, yaw_progress; F_mt = move_turn: facing_closed, yaw_progress; T = fwd, side, back, diag: ratio; Q (motion quality) = stand: every stand-applicable quality metric (action_jitter, action_fft_freq, joint_speed_mean, rod_speed_mean, contact_switch_hz, foot_slip, wz_active_frac, clock_restarts, six_down_frac, settle_six_down_s, foot_disp_end, work_per_s); fwd, side, back, diag: action_jitter, swings_per_m, slip_per_m, work_per_m, cam_work_per_m; turn, move_turn: action_jitter, swings_per_rad, slip_per_rad, work_per_rad, cam_work_per_rad. Every Q member is LOWER-is-better except six_down_frac (eval_categories.metric_sign): each delta is sign x (candidate - control), so z > R is BETTER in every block. The per-second rates of the moving categories (joint_speed_mean, rod_speed_mean, contact_switch_hz, action_fft_freq, wz_active_frac, clock_restarts, foot_slip) are WATCH there -- a slower gait lowers them without being quieter. Guards (99 %, one-sided): the survival of every present category; move_turn.ratio; fwd, side, back, diag: ratio (the speed guard -- "shuffles slower" must not pass as "quieter"; D12 let side 0.521 -> 0.430 through T as a TIE) and slip_per_m (a gait that swings less but drags its feet must not win Q); each resolved under its own guard key (cat.<c>.<key>@guard) although the metric is also a T / Q member. cat_tripod_min is NOT a guard (user decision 2026-09-22): tripod is WATCH on fwd, side, back, diag, move_turn. R_i = max(R_eval,i, R_seed,i) (+ R_binom for the survival guards); z_b = mean_i(delta_i / R_i); R_b = max(R_b^eval, R_b^seed). Per block: BETTER if z > R, WORSE if z < -R, else TIE. ADOPTION (adopt_requires: Q): ADOPT requires Q BETTER. Clear REJECT = any block or guard WORSE; or Q TIE while another block is BETTER (a win without quieting is not this campaign's goal); or all-TIE, Q included (no seed-2 pair); or a stage floor. Q BETTER + nothing WORSE + anchored drift OK + no MISSING member = clear ADOPT; Q BETTER with a MISSING member or a drift FAIL = speculative, pair queued, and the pooled decision again requires pooled Q BETTER. A MISSING guard -> decided REJECT, uncertain, no pair. WATCH, never scored: tripod, the moving categories' per-second rates, direction_error, cross_track_ratio, heading_final, settle_s, stand.drift_speed, both hands of every paired category, every per_category.demoted member (with its reason) and the legacy pooled keys.

entries.question: Is the saturated exploration noise the root of the extra motion (plan cause 1)? X08:c6's raw std sits at 2.0001-2.0004 on all 18 dimensions, at the 2.0 clamp whose gradient is zero, so the action-rate penalty is near a constant and the policy trains amid violent dither. Reset the std to 0.4 on the fork and clamp it at 0.5 (the literature's best is sigma 0.1-0.5). The reset sits BELOW the clamp on purpose: the step-2 smoke measured that a reset EQUAL to the clamp drifts straight back above it, where the clamp's gradient is zero again and the std is pinned at the ceiling -- the saturation the knob exists to undo.
